subject: Purchase-ID sequencing and spend fence for Acme Systems onboarding
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmesys.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmesys.com
Date: 2026-07-12T09:12:21+01:00
Subject: Vendor setup: Acme Systems - purchase id sequencing and spend fence

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this on. We're kicking off Redwood as a preferred inference provider and need the vendor onboarding to move quickly. Two asks to get procurement aligned:

1) Is there a provisional Purchase ID you can issue so we can start submitting invoices? Our accounting team requires a formal purchase identifier tied to a spend cap while our internal PO is approved.

2) We need confirmation of how you expect line items to be split — we'll submit three bundles (Core API calls, Dedicated capacity, Professional services) and want to avoid having line quantities merged in your ledger.

I've attached our vendor form (ACME-W9.pdf) and can pull together VAT / tax IDs if needed. Ideal timeline: provisional PO this week, final issuance next week.

Can you confirm the minimum metadata Redwood needs to bootstrap?

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Procurement | Acme Systems
procurement@acmesys.com

Attachment: ACME-W9.pdf (application/pdf, 132KB)

From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmesys.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-12T11:05:03+01:00
Subject: RE: Vendor setup: Acme Systems - purchase id sequencing and spend fence

Thanks Samir — welcome aboard.

Short answers up front: we can provision a provisional Purchase ID (P-2026-ACM-0034) and set a temporary "spend fence" while legal completes the SOW/contract. To avoid ledger merging, we prefer three explicit line items from your side with the following required metadata for each line: ledger_code, product_family (api|dedicated|services), currency, unit_quantity, expected_monthly_spend.

Action items for Acme:
- Confirm legal entity name and VAT (for EU invoicing).
- Confirm expected monthly burn per bundle (e.g., 20k EUR api / 30k EUR dedicated / 10k EUR services).
- Send the signed vendor form back (we got the W9).

On our side Monica will create a provisional Purchase ID and snapshot the ledger to validate the mapping. David will scope the spend fence (we typically start provisional caps at 60k EUR for pilots in your region, with an option to request a higher provisional limit if you provide forecasted token volume).

Attaching our onboarding checklist to make the mapping explicit. Once you return the filled vendor form and the per-bundle spend, we should be able to issue the provisional PO same day. Final PO follows legal sign-off.

Thanks — Mark
Markus Klein
Head of Channel Sales | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachment: vendor-onboard-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 18KB)

From: monica.patel@redwood.com <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-13T08:47:59+01:00
Subject: INTERNAL: provisional PID created, ledger mismatch flagged (P-2026-ACM-0034)

Markus / David — internal note (not yet sent to Acme):

I've generated provisional Purchase ID P-2026-ACM-0034 in the procurement system. When I attempted to attach the default ledger mapping to the three requested line items, the ledger reconciliation check raised a SKU/ledger mismatch for the "dedicated capacity" bucket — appears our ledger expects a product code 42-DED rather than the 40-DK that the sales mapping assumes.

Next steps I recommend:
- Hold on issuing the final PO until we confirm the ledger code mapping with finance.
- For now, we can still issue the provisional PID with a hard spend fence of 60,000 EUR and a note: "Line items pending ledger reconciliation: dedicated capacity". This will allow Acme to invoice against the provisional PID for API and Services buckets while we fix the ledger.
- Ask Acme to supply per-bundle forecast (monthly) so we can justify increasing the provisional cap if needed.

I've attached a small ledger snapshot that shows the expected codes. David — can you take the lead to align with Finance and confirm whether a temporary alias mapping (40-DK -> 42-DED) is acceptable for this onboarding? If Finance says no, we'll need to request a temporary manual allocation on next week's batch run.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: ledger-snapshot-20260713.csv (text/csv, 6KB)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmesys.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmesys.com
Date: 2026-07-15T11:03:07+01:00
Subject: RE: Vendor setup: Acme Systems - purchase id sequencing and spend fence

Thanks — appreciate the rapid turnaround.

We've filled the onboarding form (attached acme-vendor-form-2026-07-14.pdf) and included forecasted monthly spend per bundle: API 18,000 EUR / Dedicated 28,000 EUR / Services 8,000 EUR. VAT number included in the form.

Two quick Qs:
1) If you issue the provisional PID with the 60k EUR spend fence and the dedicated line is flagged, can Acme still submit API invoices immediately or will the system block against line-level mismatches? We prefer API billing to begin while you reconcile ledger codes.
2) Rough ETA on the alias mapping or manual allocation? We need to advise internal finance on when invoices will be accepted.

If it helps I'm happy to loop in our finance lead (Lindsey Cole) to provide the detailed forecast sheet.

Best regards,
Samir

Attachment: acme-vendor-form-2026-07-14.pdf (application/pdf, 48KB)
